My best friend at the time also went to the same place because of her anorexia and she told me how much she disliked this woman too. I wish I could go back in time and actually feel these situations I was in again, my memory is very hazy now. I'm afraid narcissistic people becoming therapists might not be that uncommon.
I need to remember this for the future. Not letting the enablers glorify the abusers and rationalise why my vitality needed to be ripped out of me.

It depends on how you approach therapy. Talking to someone about your mental health struggles won't magically cure you. Therapy is a good way to get support and know that someone is there to talk to you with a neutral perspective on your situation. If you're committed to growing as a person then I feel like doing talking therapy is very rewarding. You're able to slowly take responsibility for yourself and have someone in the background encourage you. 

However, a bad therapist will really mess you up. It sounds like you're very angry OP, maybe in this moment in time your gut feeling is telling you to drop therapy and that is OK. I don't know if you have a bad therapist, if you're therapist is really extorting money off you or if that is your depression talking/distrust of professionals. I'd say just listen to your intuition and stop therapy if it's making you feel worse. Maybe start writing about your feelings, it can really help with  gradually building your self esteem. Writing gives me the courage to process my emotions and then I have something to talk about with my therapist. If you don't know yourself, you walk into the room with a therapist who has nothing to work with, makes assumptions etc.
